newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish bonds seen stabilising in sellers' market.
newsitem.headline: Danish bonds seen stabilising in sellers' market.

text.p: Danish bond prices fell on Thursday but were seen stabilising by dealers after initial gains in a market dominated by sellers ahead of U.S. data.
"We could well follow Wednesday's pattern with early gains followed by falls which bottom out in the afternoon. The benchmark seems to have hit solid ground," one dealer said.

Dealers said the afternoon's U.S. new unemployed data were in focus and Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan's Senate speech would be watched with interest for indications of the direction of the American economy.

The benchmark eight percent state bond due 2006 was 0.12 down from the opening at 110.13, yielding 6.49 percent in turnover of 424 million crowns while its March future rose 0.07 point to 109.62 with 15 contracts traded.

The six percent mortgage bond due 2026 gained 0.42 point to 87.30. The crown traded at an unchanged 3.8159 per mark at 1145 gmt. The 10-year yield gap with Germany widened one basis point to 70. The Central Bank was active on the market selling around 100 million crowns worth of seven percent 2004 state bonds as part of its routine financing operations.
